newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GROWTH SEEN BROADER BASED IN 1997 - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GROWTH SEEN BROADER BASED IN 1997 - REPORT.

text.p: Poland's economic growth, fuelled by domestic demand in 1996, is likely to become broader based this year with exports picking up, Merrill Lynch said in a monthly report released on Tuesday.

"In 1997 we expect economic growth, increasingly broader based, will continue to be driven by domestic demand while exporters are expected to have a better year," it said in its January European emerging markets review.

It said the performance of Polish exports, whose growth rate fell last year because of the zloty appreciation and the weakening of Western European economies, could improve in 1997 due to a recovery of the German economy and strong demand for imported goods in Russia.
Poland's trade deficit jumped to $7.2 billion in the first 11 months of 1996 and is likely to reach $8 billion in the whole year, compared with $1.8 billion in 1995.
Merrill Lynch also said that the Polish government's 1997 target for gross domestic product growth of 5.5 percent was realistic.
It said that the central bank's concern over rising credit demand was likely to lead to a tighter monetary policy in an attempt to curb inflation.
